NOS-DOS: How to Install Applications and Games
===============================================
Version 1.0  |  NOS-DOS v1.x  |  See also: NPKG.TXT, GAMES.TXT

This guide covers everything you need to install, launch, and remove
software on NOS-DOS. Read BEFORE YOU BEGIN first, then jump to the
section for what you want to do.

CONTENTS
--------
  1. Before You Begin
  2. Installing an Application (Step by Step)
  3. Installing a Game (Step by Step)
  4. Complete Package Catalog
       Word Processing  |  Spreadsheets  |  Databases
       Programming      |  Utilities  |  Games
  5. Launching Applications
  6. Launching Games (NOSPLAY)
  7. Memory Profiles
  8. CPU Speed Presets (Games)
  9. Removing a Package
 10. Saving Files / Host File Exchange
 11. Troubleshooting


=======================================================================
1. BEFORE YOU BEGIN
=======================================================================

NETWORK CONNECTION REQUIRED
----------------------------
All packages download from the internet at install time. NOS-DOS does
not bundle copyrighted software. You must have an active network
connection before running NPKG INSTALL.

Check your connection:
  NNET STATUS              Shows your IP address and link state
  NNET DHCP                Requests an IP if none is shown
  NNET PING 8.8.8.8        Confirms internet access

If NNET STATUS shows no IP, run NNET DHCP and wait 5 seconds, then
check again. If it still fails, see Section 11 (Troubleshooting).

DISK SPACE
----------
Check available space before installing large packages:
  CHKDSK C:                Shows free bytes on C:

Space needed per category (approximate):
  Word processors, spreadsheets, utilities:   1 - 6 MB
  Databases, programming tools:               2 - 6 MB
  Games:                                      2 - 30 MB (Quake needs 30MB)

UPDATING THE PACKAGE INDEX
---------------------------
Run this once per session before installing anything new:
  NPKG UPDATE

This downloads the master package list. Without it, NPKG may not know
about packages added after your install image was built.


=======================================================================
2. INSTALLING AN APPLICATION (STEP BY STEP)
=======================================================================

Example: installing Galaxy Write (a freeware word processor).

Step 1 - Verify network:
  NNET STATUS
  (must show an IP address; if not, run NNET DHCP)

Step 2 - Update package index (once per session):
  NPKG UPDATE

Step 3 - Search for the package (optional):
  NPKG SEARCH word
  NPKG SEARCH word wordprocessing    (restrict to a category)

Step 4 - View package details (optional):
  NPKG INFO GALAXY

Step 5 - Install:
  NPKG INSTALL GALAXY

  NPKG will:
    a) Download the package definition from the repository
    b) Download the archive from archive.org (may take a few minutes)
    c) Extract to the install directory (C:\APPS\GALAXY)
    d) Run post-install setup commands
    e) Add the application to the F9 launcher in NOS-SHELL

Step 6 - Launch the application:
  From NOS-SHELL, press F9 and select it from the launcher.
  Or from the DOS prompt: GALAXY.EXE

That is all there is to it for a standard application.


=======================================================================
3. INSTALLING A GAME (STEP BY STEP)
=======================================================================

Games have additional requirements: memory profiles and CPU throttle
settings. NOSPLAY handles all of this automatically.

Example: installing DOOM Shareware.

Step 1 - Verify network and update index (same as Section 2):
  NNET STATUS
  NPKG UPDATE

Step 2 - Install:
  NPKG INSTALL DOOM

  Downloaded to: C:\GAMES\DOOM
  Archive size:  ~2.3 MB (takes 1-3 minutes on a typical VM)

Step 3 - Launch the game:
  NOSPLAY DOOM

  NOSPLAY automatically:
    a) Switches to the GAME memory profile (NOSMEM /GAME)
    b) Installs the CPU throttle TSR at SLOW33 (~33MHz)
    c) Sets the BLASTER environment variable for sound
    d) Executes the game
    e) Removes the throttle and restores the prior memory profile on exit

  Or press F9 in NOS-SHELL and select the game from the launcher.
  The F9 launcher also calls NOSPLAY for games.

Step 4 - Adjust speed if needed (while the game is running):
  Ctrl+Alt+KP+    Slow down further (higher throttle)
  Ctrl+Alt+KP-    Speed up (lower throttle)
  Ctrl+Alt+0      Disable throttle entirely

Run TCTL CALIBRATE once after first boot to ensure the speed presets
are calibrated for your virtual machine.

NOTE: Games marked "commercial" in the catalog require a legally
purchased copy of the WAD or data files. NPKG downloads from public
archive.org mirrors; you are responsible for your own licence.


=======================================================================
4. COMPLETE PACKAGE CATALOG
=======================================================================

Use NPKG INFO [ID] for full details on any package.
Use NPKG PROFILE [ID] to see hardware requirements.

WORD PROCESSING
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

GALAXY  -  Galaxy Write 4.0  (freeware)
  Install:   NPKG INSTALL GALAXY
  Location:  C:\APPS\GALAXY\
  Launch:    GALAXY.EXE
  Memory:    384 KB conventional
  Notes:     Lightweight word processor with spell checker. Good
             starting point for DOS writing. Menus via F-keys.

XYWRITE  -  XyWrite III+ v3.56  (commercial)
  Install:   NPKG INSTALL XYWRITE
  Location:  C:\APPS\XYWRITE\
  Launch:    XY.EXE
  Memory:    384 KB conventional
  Notes:     Keyboard-driven, no mouse required. Highly configurable
             via keyboard macros. Type HELP at the command line.
             Preferred by serious writers; steep learning curve.

WP51  -  WordPerfect 5.1  (commercial)
  Install:   NPKG INSTALL WP51
  Location:  C:\APPS\WP51\
  Launch:    WP.EXE
  Memory:    384 KB conventional
  Notes:     The industry standard DOS word processor. Function key
             driven. F1=Help, F3=Exit, Alt+F3=Reveal Codes.
             Requires a valid commercial licence.

WSTAR7  -  WordStar 7.0  (commercial)
  Install:   NPKG INSTALL WSTAR7
  Location:  C:\APPS\WSTAR7\
  Launch:    WS.EXE
  Memory:    384 KB conventional
  Notes:     Classic diamond-key navigation (Ctrl+E/S/D/X). F1=Help.
             Keyboard layout designed for original IBM PC without
             cursor keys. Requires a valid commercial licence.

GAMES
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

All games are launched through NOSPLAY which sets the correct memory
profile, CPU speed, and sound environment automatically.
See Section 6 for detailed NOSPLAY instructions.

KEEN1  -  Commander Keen: Marooned on Mars v1.31  (shareware)
  Install:   NPKG INSTALL KEEN1
  Location:  C:\GAMES\KEEN1\
  Launch:    NOSPLAY KEEN1  (or F9 launcher)
  Memory:    512 KB conventional
  CPU Preset: SLOW477  (~4.77 MHz)
  Notes:     EGA side-scrolling platformer. EXTREMELY speed-sensitive:
             SLOW477 is required or the game runs unplayably fast.
             Controls: Arrow keys=move, Ctrl=jump, Alt=shoot/pogo.
             No XMS required.

=======================================================================
5. LAUNCHING APPLICATIONS
=======================================================================

From NOS-SHELL (the normal way):
  Press F9 to open the application launcher.
  Use arrow keys to select, Enter to launch.
  Any package with a [LAUNCHER] section appears here automatically
  after NPKG INSTALL.

From the DOS prompt:
  Press F12 in NOS-SHELL to drop to a DOS prompt.
  Type the executable path directly, e.g.:
    C:\APPS\GALAXY\GALAXY.EXE
  Packages installed with SetPath=yes can be run by name alone:
    GALAXY
  Type EXIT to return to NOS-SHELL.

List all installed packages:
  NPKG LIST

Find where a package is installed:
  NPKG INFO [id]


=======================================================================
6. LAUNCHING GAMES (NOSPLAY)
=======================================================================

Always use NOSPLAY to launch games. Running game executables directly
will bypass the memory profile and CPU throttle setup, and the game
may crash, run at the wrong speed, or have no sound.

Basic usage:
  NOSPLAY              Interactive selector (lists installed games)
  NOSPLAY DOOM         Launch DOOM directly
  NOSPLAY INFO DOOM    Show profile details without launching

What NOSPLAY does before launching:
  1. Reads the [GAME] section from the package definition
  2. Runs NOSMEM with the correct profile (STD/MAX/EMS/GAME)
  3. Installs THROTTLE TSR at the correct CPUPreset
  4. Sets the BLASTER environment variable from SoundEnv=
  5. Changes to the game directory
  6. Runs the game executable
  7. On return: removes THROTTLE, restores prior memory profile

Live speed adjustment during a game:
  Ctrl+Alt+KP+    Increase throttle (run slower)
  Ctrl+Alt+KP-    Decrease throttle (run faster)
  Ctrl+Alt+0      Disable throttle completely

Calibrate speed presets (run once after first boot):
  TCTL CALIBRATE

Check current throttle:
  TCTL STATUS

Set throttle manually:
  TCTL SET SLOW33
  TCTL SET OFF


=======================================================================
7. MEMORY PROFILES
=======================================================================

NOSMEM switches between four preset configurations by rewriting
CONFIG.SYS and AUTOEXEC.BAT and rebooting the memory manager.
NOSPLAY calls NOSMEM automatically; you only need this manually
if you are running programs outside of NOSPLAY.

  NOSMEM /STD    Standard profile
                   620 KB+ free conventional memory
                   All standard TSRs loaded (THROTTLE, mouse, etc.)
                   JEMMEX provides EMS and XMS

  NOSMEM /MAX    Maximum conventional profile
                   635 KB+ free conventional memory
                   Removes optional TSRs from UMBs
                   Use when a program needs every byte of conventional

  NOSMEM /EMS    EMS emphasis profile
                   JEMMEX configured to provide 2-8 MB EMS
                   Required by: Descent, FoxPro (large DB), Lotus 1-2-3
                   XMS not reduced, but EMS given priority

  NOSMEM /GAME   Game profile
                   Maximum conventional + maximum XMS available
                   Only sound and mouse TSRs loaded
                   Required by: DOOM, DOOM2, Heretic, Quake, Duke3D
                   620+ KB conventional; all remaining RAM as XMS

Check current memory:
  MEM /C               Detailed memory map
  MEM /C | MORE        Paginated (press Space for next page)

Rule of thumb: if a game manual says it requires XMS, use /GAME.
If it says EMS, use /EMS. If it says nothing special, use /STD.


=======================================================================
8. CPU SPEED PRESETS (GAMES)
=======================================================================

DOS games from the 1980s and early 1990s are timing-sensitive: they
were written for specific CPU speeds. Running them on a fast VM without
throttling causes them to run at many times the intended speed.

NOSPLAY applies the correct preset automatically. Use TCTL to adjust
manually if a game runs too fast or too slow.

  Preset    Target Speed    Era             Games
  --------  ------------    ---             -----
  SLOW477   ~4.77 MHz       XT (1981-1989)  Commander Keen, Prince of
                                            Persia, early EGA games
  SLOW10    ~10 MHz         286 (1984-1990) Early 286-era titles
  SLOW33    ~33 MHz         386/486 (1992)  DOOM, Wolf3D, Heretic,
                                            Descent, Wolfenstein
  SLOW66    ~66 MHz         486 (1994-1996) DOOM II, Duke3D, Quake,
                                            Dark Forces era
  SLOW100   ~100 MHz        Pentium (1996+) Late DOS, most 1996 titles
  OFF       No throttle     Any             Freeware, modern DOS ports,
                                            Tyrian, non-timing games

If a game runs too fast after using NOSPLAY, press Ctrl+Alt+KP+ to
add more throttle. If it runs too slowly, press Ctrl+Alt+KP-.

Run TCTL CALIBRATE once after first boot to tune the presets to your
specific VM and host CPU.


=======================================================================
9. REMOVING A PACKAGE
=======================================================================

  NPKG REMOVE [id]

Example:
  NPKG REMOVE DOOM

NPKG will:
  1. Show the install directory and ask for confirmation (Y/N)
  2. Run the [REMOVE] section of the package definition (typically
     DELTREE /Y C:\GAMES\DOOM -- deletes all installed files)
  3. Remove the AUTOEXEC.BAT block that NPKG added at install time
  4. Remove the launcher entry from the F9 menu
  5. Deregister the package from INSTALLED.DB

Check what is installed before removing:
  NPKG LIST

NOTE: NPKG REMOVE deletes all installed files including save games.
Back up saves to H:\OUTBOX\ before removing a game:
  COPY C:\GAMES\DOOM\SAVE\*.* H:\OUTBOX\


=======================================================================
10. SAVING FILES / HOST FILE EXCHANGE
=======================================================================

NOS-BRIDGE mounts a shared folder from your host as H:\ (drive H).
This lets you move files between DOS and your host OS.

Set up H:\ (once per session):
  NBRIDGE MOUNT        Auto-detect and mount the shared folder
  NBRIDGE DIRS         Create INBOX, OUTBOX, PRINT, and CLIP

Copy files from DOS to your host:
  COPY C:\USER\MYFILE.TXT H:\OUTBOX\

Copy files from your host to DOS:
  (Place files in the shared folder's INBOX directory on the host)
  COPY H:\INBOX\MYFILE.TXT C:\USER\

Back up game saves before removing a game:
  COPY C:\GAMES\DOOM\SAVE\*.* H:\OUTBOX\

Check bridge status:
  NBRIDGE STATUS

On the host side: run watch_outbox.py from the host_helpers/ folder
to automatically collect files dropped in the OUTBOX.


=======================================================================
11. TROUBLESHOOTING
=======================================================================

PROBLEM: NPKG says "No network / cannot connect"
  Solution: Run NNET DHCP, wait 5 seconds, then NNET STATUS.
            If still no IP, check VM network adapter settings.
            The adapter must be set to NAT or Bridged, not Host-only.

PROBLEM: Download fails or archive is corrupt
  Solution: NPKG retries each URL 3 times. If all fail, wait 1-2
            minutes (archive.org rate limits) and run NPKG INSTALL
            again. NPKG resumes from scratch but will re-try mirrors.
            Check connectivity: NNET PING 8.8.8.8

PROBLEM: "File too small -- server returned error page"
  Solution: archive.org occasionally returns an HTML error page
            instead of the file. Wait 2 minutes and retry.
            Try: NPKG INFO [id] to see alternate URLs.

PROBLEM: "Not enough memory" when running a game
  Solution: Run NOSMEM /GAME from the DOS prompt, then NOSPLAY [id].
            If you already used NOSPLAY, check MEM /C output.
            If conventional memory is below 530 KB, something extra
            is loaded. Type NOSMEM /MAX and try again.

PROBLEM: Game requires EMS but EMS is not available
  Solution: Run NOSMEM /EMS first, then launch the game.
            NOSPLAY handles this automatically for Descent.
            Check EMS: MEM /C  (look for "EMS" line)

PROBLEM: Game runs too fast
  Solution: While the game is running, press Ctrl+Alt+KP+ to add
            more throttle. Or quit and run: TCTL CALIBRATE first,
            then NOSPLAY [id] again.

PROBLEM: Game has no sound
  Solution: Check the BLASTER environment variable:
              TYPE C:\AUTOEXEC.BAT | FIND "BLASTER"
            It should show: A220 I5 D1 H5 P330 T6
            NOS-DETECT sets this on first boot. If absent, run:
              NOSDETECT
            Then reboot and try again.

PROBLEM: "Package not found"
  Solution: Run NPKG UPDATE first to refresh the package index.
            Check spelling: NPKG SEARCH [partial name]
            IDs are case-insensitive: DOOM, doom, Doom all work.

PROBLEM: Disk full during install
  Solution: Check space: CHKDSK C:
            Remove an existing package to free space: NPKG REMOVE [id]
            Large games (Quake) need 30 MB free.

PROBLEM: NPKG LIST shows a package but NPKG REMOVE fails
  Solution: The package definition may be missing from the cache.
            Run NPKG UPDATE, then retry NPKG REMOVE [id].

For all other issues, check NPKG.TXT and GAMES.TXT for additional
command reference and game-specific compatibility notes.
